caption: The drawing depicts a single bronze or copper vessel, likely a cauldron or pot, with a rounded body that tapers slightly towards a flat, circular base. The surface of the vessel is textured with a pattern resembling hammer marks or spots. The cauldron has two outsize, looped handles that start at the rim on opposite sides, each handle rising upward in a wavy fashion and looping outward and then back again before joining the rim. The handles appear to be made of the same metal as the vessel and are affixed using round rings. The dominant color of the vessel and handles is a reddish-brown with areas of darker and lighter shading, suggesting a metallic sheen and aged patina. The background is plain and uncolored, and there are small handwritten notations, including a name and pagination, in the lower right area outside the vessel.
title: Holy-Water Bucket
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
